lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Born again to a living hope
nodes.d: Peter blesses God who by the resurrection of Jesus has given new birth to a living hope and an inheritance kept in heaven, while faith is tested like gold and the prophets searched out this salvation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what living hope Peter says believers have and why they can rejoice in trials?
ev: Describe the inheritance in 1:4
Explain why trials test faith in 1:6-7
Say what the prophets searched into in 1:10-11

nodes.t: 1 Peter: overview
nodes.d: 1 Peter is a letter from the apostle Peter to scattered strangers in Asia Minor, written to encourage them in suffering with the living hope, the example of Christ, holy conduct and humility under God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how 1 Peter encourages believers who suffer?
ev: Say who wrote 1 Peter and to whom
Name the main themes: hope, holiness, suffering and humility

nodes.t: Be holy: redeemed by precious blood
nodes.d: Peter calls believers to be holy as God is holy, reminds them they were redeemed by the precious blood of Christ the lamb without blemish, and says they were born again by the abiding word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Peter says paid the price for believers, and how they should live because of it?
ev: Say what Peter says redeemed them and what it was not
Explain the call to be holy in 1:15-16
Describe what the word of the Lord does according to 1:23-25

nodes.t: The living stone and the holy priesthood
nodes.d: Peter calls Christ the living stone chosen by God, says believers are built up as a spiritual house and royal priesthood, and says they were once not a people but are now the people of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three things Peter calls believers in 1 Peter 2:9?
ev: Explain the stone picture in 2:4-8
List the names Peter gives believers in 2:9
Say what 2:10 says changed for them

nodes.t: Strangers and pilgrims: honourable conduct and submission
nodes.d: Peter tells believers living as pilgrims among Gentiles to keep honest conduct, submit to rulers and honour all, and servants to be subject to masters even when treated wrongly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Peter says believers should behave under authorities?
ev: Say why Peter tells them to keep honest conduct among the Gentiles
Describe how Peter says to treat the king and all men

nodes.t: Christ suffered for us, an example
nodes.d: Peter says believers are called to follow the steps of Christ, who did not sin, did not revile in return, bore our sins on the tree, and brings the strayed sheep back to the Shepherd.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain both what Christ did for us and what example he left in 1 Peter 2:21-25?
ev: Describe how Christ responded when reviled
Say what Christ did on the tree in 2:24
Explain the sheep and Shepherd picture

nodes.t: Wives, husbands and the hidden person of the heart
nodes.d: Peter addresses wives with the example of Sarah and holy women, stressing a meek and quiet spirit as precious to God, and tells husbands to live with their wives with understanding and honour as fellow heirs of the grace of life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Peter tells husbands and wives in 1 Peter 3:1-7?
ev: Say what Peter calls the adorning of great price
Describe what husbands are told in 3:7

nodes.t: Blessing, good conscience and suffering for doing good
nodes.d: Peter tells all to be of one mind and repay evil with blessing, says suffering for righteousness is blessed, and that believers should always be ready to give a reason for their hope with meekness and a good conscience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Peter says to respond when others speak evil of us?
ev: Say how Peter tells believers to answer evil
Explain what being ready to answer for hope looks like in 3:15

nodes.t: Christ suffered once, the days of Noah and baptism
nodes.d: Peter says Christ suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, to bring us to God, and was made alive; he mentions the spirits who were disobedient in the days of Noah, the eight saved by water, and says baptism saves by the resurrection of Jesus, who is now at God's right hand.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Peter 3:18-22 says about Christ and about Noah?
ev: Say why Christ suffered once according to 3:18
Retell what 3:20 says about Noah and the eight saved through water
State where Christ is now according to 3:22

nodes.t: Living to the will of God
nodes.d: Peter says believers who have the mind of Christ in suffering should end the old life of Gentile excess, live to God, and prepare for the end by prayer, fervent love, hospitality and using gifts for God's glory.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list how Peter says to live because the end of all things is at hand?
ev: Describe the old life Peter says to leave behind
List the commands in 4:7-11
Explain why gifts are to be used for God's glory

nodes.t: The fiery trial and suffering as a Christian
nodes.d: Peter says not to be surprised by fiery trial but to rejoice in sharing Christ's sufferings, not to suffer as an evildoer, and to entrust the soul to a faithful Creator while judgment begins at the house of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says not to be surprised by a fiery trial?
ev: Say how Peter tells believers to view fiery trials
Distinguish suffering as a Christian from suffering as an evildoer
Say whom believers entrust their souls to in 4:19

nodes.t: Shepherd the flock, humility and the roaring lion
nodes.d: Peter exhorts elders to shepherd willingly as examples with the chief Shepherd coming, tells all to be clothed with humility, cast cares on God, resist the devil who prowls like a roaring lion, and ends with greetings from Babylon.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Peter tells elders and everyone else to do in chapter 5?
ev: Describe how elders are to lead in 5:2-3
Say what Peter tells believers to do with their cares
Say how Peter describes the devil and how to resist him

nodes.t: Genesis: overview
nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.t: Noah and the flood
nodes.d: God sees the wickedness of man, finds favour with Noah, and saves him and his household in the ark through the flood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Noah and the ark?
ev: Retell why God sent the flood and how Noah and his family were saved
Say how Noah left the ark and what he did (8:20)

nodes.t: The LORD visits Abraham and Sarah
nodes.d: The LORD appears to Abraham in the plains of Mamre as three men; Abraham hurries to feed them. One says Sarah will have a son at the appointed time, Sarah laughs inside the tent, and the LORD asks whether anything is too hard for Him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the visitors promised Sarah and why she laughed?
ev: Describe Abraham's hospitality to the three men (18:2-8)
Repeat the question the LORD asks in 18:14 and say what it is about

nodes.t: At Sinai: a kingdom of priests
nodes.d: In the third month Israel reaches Sinai. God reminds them how he bore them on eagles' wings and says that if they obey his voice and keep his covenant they will be his peculiar treasure, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. The people answer together that they will do all the LORD has spoken.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what God offered Israel at Sinai in 19:5-6 and how the people answered?
ev: Say what God reminded Israel of (19:4)
Say what God said Israel would be if they obeyed and kept his covenant (19:5-6)
Say how the people answered (19:8)

nodes.t: "Ye shall be holy": laws for neighbours
nodes.d: Leviticus 19 gathers commands under the call to be holy because the LORD is holy: honouring parents, sabbaths, leaving gleanings for the poor, honest dealing, no partiality, loving one's neighbour as oneself, care for the stranger and just weights.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list some ways Leviticus 19 says holiness shows up in daily life?
ev: Name at least five commands from the chapter that deal with how to treat other people.
Find the command to love the neighbour (19:18) and the command about the stranger (19:33-34).

nodes.t: Psalms: overview
nodes.d: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers addressed to or about the LORD: cries for help, confession, thanksgiving, praise of his creation and rule, songs about the king, and meditation on his law; the book closes with calls to praise (146-150).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three kinds of psalm and read one verse from a psalm of each kind?
ev: Name several kinds of psalm (lament, thanksgiving, praise, royal, wisdom) and give one psalm number for each.

nodes.t: Psalm 34: taste and see that the LORD is good
nodes.d: The speaker blesses the LORD at all times, tells how this poor man cried and the LORD saved him, says the angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear him, teaches children the fear of the LORD, and says the LORD is near the broken-hearted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Psalm 34 teaches about crying to the LORD and what children are taught in 34:11-14?
ev: Read 34:1-10 and 34:11-14 and list what the speaker teaches the children.

nodes.t: Psalms 117-118: his mercy endureth for ever; the stone the builders refused
nodes.d: Psalm 117 calls all nations to praise the LORD for his great mercy and truth; Psalm 118 calls Israel to say his mercy endures for ever, tells of being delivered from distress, says it is better to trust the LORD than man, speaks of the stone the builders refused, and ends with giving thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the refrain “his mercy endureth for ever” and the picture in Psalm 118:22-23?
ev: Read 118:5-9, 118:19-24 and 118:26-29 and list what is said about the LORD and the gate.

nodes.t: Proverbs: overview
nodes.d: Proverbs begins with the proverbs of Solomon son of David (1:1), sets out a father’s teaching about wisdom and folly (1-9), gathers many short sayings (10-29), and ends with the words of Agur (30) and of king Lemuel (31).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the main sections of Proverbs and who is named as the source of each?
ev: Describe the main sections of Proverbs: 1-9, 10-22, 22-24, 25-29, 30, 31.

nodes.t: Trust in the LORD with all your heart
nodes.d: The father tells his son to keep his commandments, trust in the LORD and not lean on his own understanding, accept the LORD’s correction, value wisdom above silver and gold, and do good to his neighbour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 3:5-6 and give one example of leaning on one’s own understanding?
ev: Read 3:5-6 and say what the son is told to do and what the LORD does.
Find 3:11-12 and say what it says about correction.

nodes.t: Proverbs of Solomon: the righteous, the wicked and words (10-11)
nodes.d: Short sayings contrast the righteous and the wicked, the diligent and the lazy, and the mouth that gives life with the mouth that harms; chapter 11 adds sayings on integrity, pride, surety and generosity.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} pick one saying from Proverbs 10 or 11 and explain what two ways of life it contrasts?
ev: Collect three contrasts between righteous and wicked from chapter 10 and chapter 11.

nodes.t: Isaiah: overview
nodes.d: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?
ev: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts

nodes.t: Maher-shalal-hash-baz and the Assyrian flood
nodes.d: Isaiah writes a name-sign for a son, the LORD warns that the king of Assyria will flood Judah, tells Isaiah not to fear what the people fear, and calls him to the law and testimony instead of mediums.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD says to sanctify him rather than fear what the people fear in Isaiah 8:11-13?
ev: Explain the meaning of the child's name sign in 8:1-4
Say whom Isaiah is told to fear and sanctify (8:12-13)
Explain the contrast between the law and testimony and consulting the dead (8:19-20)

nodes.t: Woe to Ephraim's drunkards and the scoffers in Jerusalem
nodes.d: Isaiah rebukes the drunken leaders, who mock his teaching, boast of a covenant with death, and are promised a tested cornerstone laid in Zion; the farmer's patient work illustrates God's wise ways.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the scoffers in Isaiah 28:15 relied on and what the LORD lays in Zion in 28:16?
ev: Describe the scoffers' covenant with death (28:15)
Quote what the LORD lays in Zion (28:16)
Explain the farmer illustration in 28:23-29

nodes.t: Comfort my people: the incomparable God
nodes.d: God tells his prophets to comfort Jerusalem because her iniquity is pardoned, a voice prepares the way of the LORD, the LORD comes as shepherd, and no one compares to him who gives strength to the weary.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD comforts Jerusalem in Isaiah 40:1-2 and who the LORD is compared to in 40:12-26?
ev: Quote the command and reason in Isaiah 40:1-2
Describe the voice crying in the wilderness (40:3-5)
Explain what 40:28-31 says about those who wait on the LORD

nodes.t: The servant exalted, despised and bearing iniquity
nodes.d: The servant is high, yet marred; despised and rejected, he bears griefs and iniquities of others, is wounded for transgressions and led like a lamb, is cut off and buried with the rich, and after his soul's travail justifies many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the servant suffers and for whose sake according to Isaiah 53:4-6?
ev: Describe what Isaiah 53:4-6 says he bears and for whom
Describe how he is treated (53:3, 7-9)
Say what the LORD says follows in 53:10-12

nodes.t: Hosea: overview
nodes.d: Hosea's word to Israel in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash and Judah's kings: a prophet's marriage to an unfaithful wife pictures the LORD's love for faithless Israel, followed by charges, judgment and a call to return.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences how Hosea's marriage pictures the LORD's relationship with Israel?
ev: Say that Hosea's marriage (chs 1-3) is an acted picture of the LORD and Israel
Outline the book as marriage (1-3), charges and judgment (4-13) and a closing call to return (14)

nodes.t: The LORD pleads and allures his wife
nodes.d: The LORD charges Israel with going after her lovers and forgetting him, announces discipline, then promises to allure her into the wilderness and betroth her to himself for ever in faithfulness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how chapter 2 moves from judgment on Israel to the LORD betrothing her again?
ev: Describe the charge (2:5, 2:8, 2:13) and the discipline (2:6-13)
Describe the promise to betroth Israel for ever (2:19-20) and to say 'Thou art my people' (2:23)
